title: ThruLines #009
phrase: For well you know that it's a fool who plays it cool

questions.subject: Music
questions.prompt: According to Elton John, these types of songs “say so much”.
questions.connectionNote: Take a sad song and make it better — the whole mission statement of the song.

questions.subject: Life
questions.prompt: What's it called when a married couple officially calls it quits?
questions.connectionNote: Paul wrote it driving out to comfort five-year-old Julian Lennon during John and Cynthia's divorce.

questions.subject: Cars
questions.prompt: Which popular Volkswagen model shares its name with an insect?
questions.connectionNote: The Beetle — one letter off the band that made this the biggest single of 1968.

questions.subject: Television
questions.prompt: What's the last name of Bryan Cranston's character in Breaking Bad?
questions.connectionNote: White — recorded in 1968, the same sessions and summer as The White Album.

questions.subject: Movies
questions.prompt: What was Wes Anderson's third feature film?
questions.connectionNote: The film opens on an instrumental 'Hey Jude' — Anderson built the whole introduction of the Tenenbaum children around it.

reveal.summary: Hey Jude. Sad songs say so much — and this one exists to take a sad song and make it better. The divorce is the one Paul drove out to soften for little Julian Lennon, the Beetle is one letter off the band, White is the album summer it was born in, and The Royal Tenenbaums opens on the song itself. The line is the song's quiet center: don't play it cool.
reveal.ohMoment: Elton was pointing at the mission statement all along — take a sad song and make it better.

editorial.notes: Playtest revision: swapped out the Sha Na Na question (too obscure) and the golf 'Fore' question (misread as a trick) for Elton John's sad songs (points at 'take a sad song and make it better') and the VW Beetle (one letter off the band). Phrase trimmed at the rhyme break (40 letters).
